text:
riley: putting up a short thread about snapshot consistency for runtime hints. ran into a weird edge where edges running different snapshot bases admitted divergent candidate sets. want to align on safety model and recovery behaviours.
hao: can you describe the observed divergence?
riley: sure — scenario: compiler emits base S@100 then delta D1, D2. edge A applied both deltas, edge B missed D2. runtime filter on B removed a route that the compiled policy would later require during final adjudication -> extra fallback to slower region.
devika: that matches our fear. what's the safety invariant we care about?
riley: primary invariant: runtime filters must never create a state where no valid compiled route remains. we can be conservative by design: runtime can only remove routes if the compiled snapshot says they are removable. but with missing deltas that's violated.
hao: sounds like either we need strong ordering guarantees for deltas, or a conservative default. which do we prefer?
devika: strong ordering at scale is painful. i vote for stateless verification + conservative fallback. runtime should verify delta_chain integrity before applying and roll back to base if anything missing.
ops: agree on rollback, but also need observability. if an edge falls back to conservative mode we must surface a paged alert for large tenant impact.
riley: proposal: delta payload includes base_hash and seq_range. runtime keeps last_applied_seq and base_hash. when receiving delta, it validates base_hash==cached_base else fetch full snapshot. if seq gap -> refuse delta and fetch full snapshot. if fetch fails -> conservative pass-through (no filters).
hao: add a reconcile timer too. runtime should periodically fetch full snapshot and compare base_hash to detect silent corruption. default reconcile every 5m.
devika: reconciliation good. also add a short conservative_window after applying a new snapshot or delta (e.g., 1s) where we bias fail-open to reduce transient false filters while other edges catch up.
ops: how will oncall troubleshoot which edge is behind? need metrics and debug endpoints.
riley: telemetry: delta_apply_success_rate, delta_gap_rejects, snapshot_fetch_failures, conservative_mode_rate, false_filter_incidents, cross_edge_inconsistency_count. add decision_signature logs with snapshot_id + seq_id + signer_id.
devika: debug API: /internal/debug/route_eval?include_compiled=true should show runtime filtered candidates + compiled final set for that request_id. protect to internal only and sample at 100% for canaries.
hao: can we tighten with optimistic apply plus validation? like apply delta tentatively, run local verifier with compiled rule hashes, and if verifier fails revert. might reduce full snapshot fetches.
riley: yes, tentative apply + local validation is neat. but verifier needs the compiled rule hashes or a compact Merkle of the snapshot. compiler can emit a merkle_root for snapshots and deltas include proofs. runtime can verify proofs cheaply.
devika: merkle approach adds complexity but worth it for bandwidth. make merkle optional at first and fall back to base_hash checks. include this in RFC as an enhancement.
ops: rollout plan?
riley: plan: 1) shadow deltas for 7d: runtime logs what-it-would-have-done, no actual pruning 2) enable delta apply on 3% of edges with reconcile and conservative windows 3) increase to 20% with heightened alerting 4) global. gating: false_filter_incidents < 0.01% and conservative_mode_rate < 2% for 24h.
devika: also add a tenant whitelist to skip runtime filters for high-risk customers. config `runtime.hints.white_list`.
hao: add a fail-safe: if compiled policy changes significantly ( >X routes changed ) treat as full snapshot and don't rely on deltas for that change. helps big churn events.
riley: good. metric: snapshot_delta_size and rule_change_ratio. default rule_change_ratio threshold 0.1.
ops: emergency ops knobs?
devika: add `runtime.hints.enabled=false`, `runtime.hints.force_full_snapshot=true` and `runtime.hints.debug_force_conservative=true`. document rollback playbook: force_full_snapshot -> disable hints -> flush caches -> revert rollout.
hao: quick config snippet for RFC:
```
runtime.hints.enabled = true
runtime.hints.delta_apply = true
runtime.hints.reconcile_interval = "5m"
runtime.hints.conservative_window_ms = 1000
runtime.hints.max_delta_gap = 0
runtime.hints.rule_change_ratio_threshold = 0.1
runtime.hints.white_list = ["tenant:acme"]
```
riley: ops-bot please create INFRA ticket to add reconcile fetch route and debug endpoint.
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-5102 "runtime-hints-snapshot-reconcile-and-debug-api". https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-5102
devika: final ask: include a CI check in the compiler to compute snapshot merkle roots and optionally provide proofs for deltas. helps with verification once we enable merkle mode.
hao: agreed. also add simulation: replay 7d traffic with intentional delta loss injected at 1% edges to validate conservative behaviour.
riley: will draft RFC with these pieces: delta proto, tentative-apply + validation, reconcile timer, metrics, debug APIs, CI merkle generation, and rollout gating. scheduling arch sync next Thurs.
ops: thanks all. make sure runbooks include contact list for paging on false_filter spikes.
riley: will do. closing thread.
